name: Es Cucons
open: Open until 15 Nov · reopens end of February
desc: Rural hotel in a 17th-century finca on the Pla de Corona, with a spa, sauna, hot tub, restaurant and live concerts. Closes mid-November and reopens at the end of February, just as the almond blossom fades — the Santa Agnès address for a late-winter weekend.

name: Las Puertas del Cielo
open: Open until 15 Nov · reopens end of February
desc: Clifftop bar-restaurant above the north-west coast, named for the 'gates of heaven' view. One of the island's great sunset spots and the natural end to the Ses Balandres walk. Closes 15 November, back at the end of February.

name: Can Cosmi
desc: The village bar-restaurant opposite the church: the island's most talked-about tortilla, lamb chops, rustic salads and a terrace in the sun. Salsa nights in winter — ask at the bar for the next one.

name: Sa Palmera
desc: Classic Spanish cooking on the village square — the locals' choice after a walk. Simple, honest plates and a terrace that catches the winter sun.

name: Ses Casetes
desc: Country restaurant on the village square: homemade island cooking, grilled meats and fish, a colourful interior, art on the walls and live concerts. Lunch in the winter sun after a walk through the Albarca vineyards.

name: Juntos House
desc: Farmhouse restaurant, shop and clubhouse: organic plates from their own land, natural wines and cocktails, plus The Pergola for walk-in drinks and tapas. Open through the holidays last winter — check their Instagram for current days.

name: Mercat de Forada — Can Tixedó
desc: The island's most local Saturday market, in the field by Can Tixedó Art Café: farm fruit and veg, homemade food, crafts, a book swap, kids' zone, vegan paella at 13:00 and the odd live set. Coffee and lunch at Tixedó afterwards.

name: La Finca Can Suldat
desc: Swiss-Ibizan finca restaurant under a vine-roofed courtyard: cheese fondue, steak, goulash and 'Peter's famous salad', with live music through the winter. Go early evening to catch the music with the locals, and book a table.

name: La Paloma
desc: An old finca among orange and lemon trees, with lunch in the flowering garden and dinners by lantern light: Italian-meets-Middle-Eastern plates, homemade bread, organic salads and a good bottle. Hours shift with the season — check their Instagram before you drive out.

name: Bar Costa
open: Open all year except March · closed Tuesdays
desc: The village institution on the square, hams hanging from the ceiling and paintings left by artists who paid in canvases. Bocadillos, tostadas and a cortado at the bar — the place the whole island passes through on a winter Sunday.

name: Bar Anita
desc: The hippie-era village bar opposite the church, with the old wooden post boxes still on the wall. Home-made hierbas, simple plates, a shaded terrace — and open every single day of the year.

name: Bar Can Berri
desc: Tiny bar on the prettiest village square in the west, under the church. Known in winter for its calçotades on Sundays in February and March: charred spring onions, romesco, grilled meat and plenty of wine.

name: Sa Carboneria
desc: Steakhouse and garden just behind the town hall: aged meats over charcoal, a warm dining room for the cold nights, a small garden for the sunny lunches. Winter weekends bring the Hunger BBQ, and Sa Carbo Bar has live music October to March — this is where The Oyster Nomad set up in October.

name: The Oyster Nomad
open: All winter · delivers and pops up
desc: A travelling oysterman — top hat, shucking knives, Umami oysters and AIX rosé — who delivers to villas and restaurants across the island all winter and shows up for pop-up nights. Shuck the world. No bar, no terrace: he comes to you.

name: Olas Gallery
desc: Photographer Sofia Gómez Fonzo's gallery and concept store a few steps from the beach: a show that changes every month, always with island artists — painting, aerial and underwater photography, cyanotypes, hand-stitched maps — and a shelf of books, prints, ceramics and oracle cards made on Ibiza. Talks and openings through the winter.
now: Autumn programme: Marcel Boer's Ibiza light studies, then Arnoud L∆L∆, and a group show of island artists in December.

name: Parra & Romero
desc: The Madrid gallery's island outpost in an industrial space on the village paseo: conceptual and minimal art, site-specific projects, the kind of show you'd expect in Chelsea, with a coffee at Bar Costa afterwards. Tue–Sat 11–14 & 16:30–20:30, Mondays 17–21.
now: Landon Metz — the Arizona painter's first solo show in Spain, opened late September.

name: MACE — Museu d'Art Contemporani
desc: One of Spain's first contemporary art museums, set into the walls of Dalt Vila with the Phoenician and Roman foundations visible under glass floors. The permanent collection is the island's art story since the 1960s; the temporary shows are the reason to go back. Winter hours: Tue–Fri 10–16:30, weekends 10–14.

name: Es Polvorí
desc: The old gunpowder store on the Santa Llúcia bastion, now the town's space for temporary shows: painting, photography and sculpture by artists living here, in a vaulted stone room with the harbour below. Tue–Fri 18–20:30, weekends 11–13:30.

name: Galería Marta Torres
desc: A gallery in the port since the 1990s: Marta Torres's own work and group shows of island painters, part of the emerging art route around La Marina. Mon–Fri 10–14.

name: Can Curt
desc: The village exhibition room opposite the church — painting, photography, sculpture, mostly by people who live within ten minutes of it. Combine with a drink at Can Berri Vell across the square. Thu–Sun 18–21.

name: Can Jeroni
desc: Sant Josep's cultural centre: exhibitions downstairs, and through the winter a programme of film, poetry, concerts and theatre that the village actually turns up for. Wed–Sun 10:30–13:30, plus Thu–Sat 18–21.

name: Sa Punta des Molí
desc: A restored windmill and olive press on the bay, with an exhibition hall and an open-air auditorium. Small shows by local artists; worth the walk along the promenade on a bright winter morning. Winter: Tuesdays and Saturdays 10–13 & 16–19.

name: Bartienne & The Cook's Atelier
open: All winter · dinners twice a month
desc: Barbara and Etienne's antique and interiors shop on the Santa Eulària road — French flea-market furniture, pieces from Asia and India, outdoor kitchens — with an open kitchen at the back. Barbara cooks there: long-table dinners for 20 to 40 a couple of weekends a month, and cooking workshops (Spanish, Italian, French) for groups. Follow @the_cooks_atelier_ibiza for the next date, or book the whole space for your own night. Carretera Santa Eulària 380.

name: Chez Bibi
desc: Café-restaurant with its own little bakery at the top of the village: Parisian croissants and cinnamon rolls, sourdough, poke and big salads, cakes that change daily. Laptops are welcome — on a grey winter morning half the terrace is working, the other half is on its second coffee. Dog-friendly, card accepted, book for lunch at weekends.
